subject: gk
question: Which of the following claims concerning the magnetic lines of force inside a bar magnet is true?

options.text: From S-pole to N-pole of the magnet
Depends on the cross-sectional area of the bar magnet
From N-pole to S-pole of the magnet

solution:
The correct answer is__** From S-pole to N-pole of the magnet.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** magnetic lines of force** inside a **bar magnet** run from the **South pole** to the **North pole** of the magnet.
 
• This is because the magnetic field is oriented in such a way that it flows from the **South pole to the North pole.**
 
• The strength of the magnetic field is **greatest** at the **poles of the magnet** and **gradually decreases **as you move away from them.
 
• The orientation of the magnetic field is determined by the orientation of the **magnetic domains **within the magnet, not its shape or size.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Magnetic lines of force are also known as **magnetic field lines **or** flux lines.**
 
• They represent the direction and** strength of the magnetic field** at each point in space.
 
• The direction of the magnetic field is defined as the **direction that a compass needle** would point if placed at that point in space.
 
• The **strength** of the magnetic field is proportional to the **density **of the magnetic field lines, with more lines indicating a** stronger field.**
 
• Magnetic fields are created by the movement of **electric charges,** such as the flow of electrons in a wire or the** spinning of electrons **within atoms.
